findings.evidence: Step 4: "subagent-driven-development's \"3. Review the task\", \"4. The fix loop\" (rounds 1–5), and the final whole-branch review run unmodified" restates line 12-14's ownership statement
findings.fix: Cut Step 4 to one line ("Review, fix loop and final review stay with subagent-driven-development; this skill resumes at Step 5") since lines 12-14 already give that ownership split

findings.evidence: "**Either branch, with a restored `$FIX_ROUND >= 4` and no pinned `injection_json`:** that plain result (any mode) is only the source of `ladder_keys`: never act on its mode or dispatch it; ..." — the resume, pin and escalation rules are packed into one paragraph instead of a phased decision
findings.fix: Turn the resume check into a short decision table (RESUME_FOUND x pinned injection_json x FIX_ROUND>=4 -> next action) so the Process pattern has explicit checkpoints

findings.evidence: Environment facts such as "subprocess dispatch needs Node 24 ... an older Node may crash" and "`.git` writes unverified" sit inside Step 3 prose rather than a Gotchas list
findings.fix: Add a short Gotchas section beside NEVER that collects the environment surprises: Node 24 floor, Codex workspace-write `.git` writes unverified, pi/copilot exec unverified, and every Bash call starts a fresh shell, so scalars must be reloaded

findings.evidence: description opens "Runs a superpowers implementation plan ..." (declarative, implementation-heavy: "resolving a live-quota-checked (runtime, model) pair")
findings.fix: Run a superpowers implementation plan (docs/superpowers/plans/*.md) under superpowers:subagent-driven-development, choosing a live-quota-checked (runtime, model) pair for each task's implementer (native subagent or external CLI such as Codex), with quota waits and fix-round model escalation; starts the plan's unit branch first and folds, pushes and readies it after the final review via ai-kit-commit-fold. Use when ai-kit-spec-execute detects a superpowers plan, or when asked to execute, run or carry out a superpowers plan task by task with subagents or per-task model choice. Not for superpowers:executing-plans (inline, no dispatch point), writing a plan, or folding a branch on its own (ai-kit-commit-fold).

findings.evidence: `references/quota-wake.md` is loaded only from dispatch-external-cli.md, a second-level reference chain; SKILL.md mentions "quota-wake" only in passing at line 157
findings.fix: Name `references/quota-wake.md` with its trigger in SKILL.md Step 3's `"quota"` bullet ("read references/quota-wake.md before scheduling or printing a wake") so every reference stays one level from SKILL.md

findings.evidence: "On another host, use its own subagent mechanism (or STOP and tell the user to resume by hand)" — a menu with no default for the non-Claude wake path
findings.fix: Pick a default: "On another host, use the Schedule-or-stop print path; STOP and tell the user to resume by hand only when the host has no subagent mechanism"

findings.evidence: Seven output evals cover the start, fold, external_cli and out-of-scope paths, but none covers quota_exhausted/no_candidate stops, the trust-local ask or Rounds 4–5 escalation; trigger queries are 9 positive / 11 negative
findings.fix: Add an eval that gives a resolve-injection result with mode quota_exhausted (assert: the run stops, writes resumable state via resume-exclusions and schedules nothing), plus one for FIX_ROUND 4 with an empty anchor (assert: it STOPs and asks the owner); swap one generic negative trigger query for a near-miss positive

findings.evidence: "(block below; new rounds only, never on a resume, a re-invoke that kept its scalars or a Step-2 re-entry, which keep the round and anchor, yet at 4 or more still take the floor below)" — nested exceptions make it hard to tell when the increment block runs
findings.fix: Replace the parenthetical with a 3-row list: new fix round -> run the increment block; resume, re-invoke or Step-2 re-entry -> skip it; any path at FIX_ROUND>=4 without a pin -> apply references/escalation.md's floor

findings.evidence: Each task-paths block makes the agent re-type six `<Step 0 ...>`/`<Step 1 ...>` placeholders by hand, and every later call needs a re-typed SCALARS literal
findings.fix: After the first task, have the task-paths block read SKILL_DIR/SHIM/TOOLS_PY/CWD/PLAN_FILE from $SCALARS and take only TASK_N as input, so later tasks have one placeholder
